text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.21% today to $137.64, continuing a steady climb over the past two weeks (+5.59%). The immediate driver is today's news that Saudi Arabia shut down a critical pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz after attacks from Iran-allied groups, which pushed oil prices higher — US crude is trading at $97.26/barrel and global oil at $109.51. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly lift earnings potential and stock value.

The broader backdrop amplifies this move: US diesel prices have hit record levels above $6 per gallon due to combined supply pressures from the Russia-Ukraine war and escalating Iran tensions, keeping energy markets tight and supportive of oil prices well above $100/barrel. These geopolitical shocks to global supply have traders betting gas prices will keep rising, which benefits integrated energy companies with production and refining operations.
